minutes.headline: Planning Board continued the 6 MW Northfield Road solar hearing to Oct 23 after criticizing buffers and fire plans.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was the continued hearing on a six-megawatt solar farm at 994 Northfield Road, with abutters and board members criticizing the buffer, fire response, decommissioning estimate and visuals. The board also approved a de minimis drainage change for Unitil, met its new town counsel, and recommended acquiring a parcel. The solar hearing was continued to October 23 with the decision deadline extended.

public_comment.topic: Board member asked about moving the flag so everyone in the room can see it (not public).
Abutter building a home at 1048 Northfield Road objects to the solar farm behind his lot, was not notified, asks why it can't be located elsewhere.
Resident on the west side (New West Townsend Road) worried about property values, water table, fire and loss of woods.
Long-time New West Townsend Road resident objects to clear-cutting, erosion, storms and fire access from his backyard.
Chair read a statement from Jerry Wilkins, 251 Bird Street, opposing large solar plants in residential areas.
Abutter says answers were lacking on fire risk, toxic emissions, property values and insurance premiums.
Neighbor who sold lots to abutters supports the owner's right but asks that the project be modified and reduced in size near the new homes.
Property owner explains the golf course business reasons for the project and asks the board to state clear conditions.
Correction to minutes: Heather Bowen's comment should say residential kitchen, not commercial.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the public hearing on a six-megawatt solar farm at 994 Northfield Road to October 23 and extended the decision deadline.
Abutters and board members criticized the project's buffer, fire response, decommissioning estimate and visuals during the continued hearing.
The peer reviewer said the applicant's decommissioning surety estimate looks low; the estimate was challenged as based on a different project.
The applicant agreed to submit revised plans by the Tuesday before the October 23 meeting.
The board voted to recommend that the town acquire a Chapter 61 parcel for open space and trail access.

why_it_matters: Residents near Northfield Road and New West Townsend Road will see the solar plan return in revised form, with buffers, fire access and the cost of removing the panels still open.

A low decommissioning estimate matters because that surety is what would pay for removal if the owner does not, and a payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement still under negotiation would set what the project pays the town.
The Chapter 61 land recommendation is likely to reach a town vote on whether to buy the parcel, which would be a cost to the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: October 23 continued hearing on 994 Northfield Road, with revised plans due the Tuesday before.
Dates for the extra bylaw workshop meeting, which Adam is to propose.
